verdict.reason: Two material findings in my scope block R7A1-FREEZE-A1, both narrow, runtime-only and pre-existing on R7A-FREEZE-2, both needing no policy text: D57 (the return cap ends against the ending week’s count and after weeks fitted below their count, so a count comes back 1 to 3 at a block boundary: a known equivalent path of D53, so D53 and D56 stay open) and D58 (a short return’s easy first quality slot does not reach the next week when this week’s quality slot is past: the QE-R7A-02 class is not closed). Everything else in my remit holds: the D56 formulation ("last") is approved, and S2 and S4-S10 are approved or ruled.

Three of the seven blockers are not closed by their mechanism (QE-R7A-01, QE-R7A-02, QE-R7A-05). Five material equivalent paths were found (QE-R7A1-01 to 05, two HIGH): a re-applied move keeps the equipment of its history; the weekly review's next-week start is re-derived without its systemic hold and confirmed loads; a return correction across the week boundary does not supersede; same-day eligibility differs between the adaptation handlers and the rest; the merge still loses a known load behind an unreadable one. Each has a minimal reproduction and a required change for the single correction cycle.

One blocking finding in my scope: D59 (new in this re-check, pre-existing since at least R7A-FREEZE-2, outside the FREEZE-A1 to A2 delta), a known equivalent state mode of D53. A moderate return whose pause week holds the first executed exposures of an exercise starts from a state that predates them; when that week is the athlete's first loaded week, every exercise executed before the break restarts as a first establishment: no return entry (672 of 672 exercises), the block in progress earns its set, 1,582 rows above the declared ceiling and 226 counts two sets above the largest since the return (NONE and FAMILIAR athletes, every case of the configuration). Under Founder request §10, D53 cannot be CLOSED while a known equivalent state mode allows a restoration jump, and §13 requires D53 CLOSED. Both findings of my first review are closed: D57 and D58. D56 is closed. S1 and S4-S10 hold at FREEZE-A2. The fix is runtime-only: no policy text, clinical semantics or Founder decision is needed for the ruling.

All five findings of the first review are closed by their mechanism, with a test that fails on FREEZE-A1 and passes on FREEZE-A2. But the mechanism of the QE-R7A1-03 fix (and the C5 rule of FREEZE-A1 it extends) does not check that a newer return reports the same break. A second, separate break that begins in a week an earlier return re-planned is treated as a correction of the first: its return starts from the state before the first break. The first return's re-entry is erased (return steps, run RETURN mode), and the athlete goes back to pre-break doses after a 16-day break: 1 set at RIR 4 becomes 3 sets at RIR 3 at the pre-break known load, and the long run goes from 20-45 to 70-75 minutes (QE-R7A1-09, HIGH, material). The same missing identity makes a second short break reuse the first one's easy slot, so its own first quality run stays hard (QE-R7A1-10, MEDIUM, material). Across the week boundary the defect is new in FREEZE-A2; inside the same week it is already present in FREEZE-A1, and my first review missed it. FREEZE-2 has neither. A new HIGH blocks under FOUNDER_REQUEST §13.
